discovery: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background using pulsar timing arrays

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany

motivation: In 2023 pulsar timing arrays reported the first evidence for a gravitational-wave background at nanohertz frequencies. The signal shows the Hellings-Downs angular correlation predicted by general relativity, and its likely source is the cosmic population of supermassive black-hole binaries. LIGO opened the audio band; this work opens a second window, about ten orders of magnitude lower in frequency, and turns the Galaxy's millisecond pulsars into a detector the size of the Galaxy. McLaughlin co-founded NANOGrav and led much of its decades-long precision timing programme. Siemens built the data-analysis, noise-modelling and statistical framework that made the result a robust measurement, and he led the collaboration through it. Kramer's pioneering precision timing of pulsars and his leadership of the European and International PTA efforts set the standard for testing gravity with pulsars. Together their work turned an experiment into an observatory, and it opens the way to studying how galaxies and black holes grow together.
